task_instance: Invoke the cortex ML/AI-engineer skill on a small sample project (a support-triage service with one LLM summarization call and a scikit-learn priority model) to produce its core deliverable. With no/unclear args the skill's stated default is to route to its cortex-recon sub-skill: inventory the project's existing models, pipelines, data sources, and monitoring.
blocker_detail: The cortex SKILL.md is only a dispatcher: it reads the request and, via the Skill tool, invokes one of five named sub-skills (cortex-eval, cortex-integrate, cortex-model, cortex-prompt, cortex-recon; cortex-recon is the no-args default). None of those five sub-skill documents are present anywhere under the skill's repository copy (the skills directory contains only cortex/SKILL.md), and none are offered in this session's available-skills list, so there is nothing to invoke. The actual methodology and deliverable format live entirely in the missing sub-skills; the dispatcher itself defines no deliverable. The run rules forbid writing my own replacement/stub for a missing skill file, so the core deliverable cannot be produced.
evidence: Read skill at skills/r185/plugins/ai-agency/tonone/skills/cortex/SKILL.md: a router that lists sub-skills cortex-eval/cortex-integrate/cortex-model/cortex-prompt/cortex-recon and instructs 'invoke the right skill with the Skill tool', default cortex-recon. Glob of skills/r185/plugins/ai-agency/tonone/skills/** returned exactly one path: cortex/SKILL.md, confirming the five referenced sub-skill files are absent. The session available-skills list contains no cortex-recon/eval/integrate/model/prompt entries. Created a realistic sample input project to run recon against at work dir sample_project/ (requirements.txt listing LLM + vector-store + sklearn deps, app/llm_client.py with a model id and prompt template, README.md noting no evals/cost-tracking/drift-monitoring).
